metaDescription: Specialist logistics and transport translation for freight, shipping and passenger services into French, German, Spanish and more. Request your free quote.
bodyHtml:
Logistics and transport translation services

December 14, 2020
Logistics | Professional Translation

Every shipment travels with paperwork. Invoices, consignment notes, customs declarations and safety instructions pass through drivers, warehouse teams, customs officers and customers, often in more than one language.

If you run a freight, courier, passenger transport or supply chain business, translation is part of how goods and people move. One unclear document can delay a load, start a dispute or leave a passenger without vital information.

BeTranslated has helped companies in the logistics sector for over 20 years. We translate from English into the main European, Scandinavian and Asian languages, including French, Italian, German, Portuguese and Spanish.

How important is translation in the logistics industry?

Logistics depends on everyone in the chain reading the same facts. UK government export guidance explains that a commercial invoice gives customs authorities the information they need to decide whether goods can move and what duties and taxes apply, and that every shipment needs its own invoice. If the people receiving that information cannot read it with confidence, the shipment stalls.

Translation also protects you commercially. Terms on liability, delivery and payment must mean the same thing in every language you trade in, or a routine claim can become a lengthy dispute.

Logistics documents we translate

We translate the commercial, legal and operational documents that move goods and people, including:

  • commercial invoices and packing lists
  • bills of lading, air waybills and consignment notes
  • customs declarations and supporting documents
  • freight, carrier and warehousing contracts
  • cargo insurance documents and claims correspondence
  • safety data sheets and health and safety instructions
  • driver, crew and warehouse procedures
  • tracking messages, delivery notices and customer service templates

Our document translation service handles each of these, and you can send several documents in one project.

Why specialist translators matter for freight and shipping

Shipping language is precise. Terms such as bill of lading, demurrage and the Incoterms rules published by the International Chamber of Commerce have exact meanings, and a general translator may render them in a way that changes your obligations.

We match your project to linguists with experience in commercial and trade documents and technical content. For regular work, we can keep your glossary and previous translations together so that terminology stays consistent from one shipment to the next.

Translation for air, rail, road and sea passenger services

If you carry passengers, your information has to work for people who do not speak English. Translated content widens your audience and helps visitors use your services safely.

Air carriers

Air travel generates a lot of text that passengers must understand, such as practical flight information, safety instructions and in-flight magazines. Our translators have a solid understanding of the demands of air transport, so your safety and service wording stays accurate in every language.

Rail and road

Many visitors take buses or trains for day trips. Translated timetables, leaflets, ticket information and activity guides make it easier for them to plan and buy, and you can reach more travellers as a result.

Ocean and river transport

Passenger cruises on the sea, canals and rivers depend on clear itineraries, excursion details and onboard safety messages. Our experts in tourism and transport translation provide the right text for each one, whether you run a canal trip or an island-hopping cruise.

Languages for logistics translation

If you trade with mainland Europe, French and German are natural places to start. Our French business translators and German business translators work in both directions between English and the target language.

We also translate into Dutch, Korean, Russian, Arabic, Hebrew and Nordic languages such as Norwegian, Danish and Swedish. If you need a language that is not listed, ask us.

How to brief a logistics translation project

A few details help us deliver a translation you can use straight away:

  • the source files in editable format
  • the destination country and who will read the document
  • any glossary, style guide or earlier translations
  • the deadline and whether the document will be updated later

If you also need to speak to overseas partners or drivers, remote interpreting can support your calls and meetings.

Our translation agency also specialises in

  • Marketing translation
  • Technical translation
  • Financial translation
  • Travel and tourism translation
  • IT translation

We quote per project. Send your documents through our quote request page and one of our project managers will come back with a free, no-obligation quote.

Frequently asked questions

Which logistics documents can you translate?

We translate invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, consignment notes, customs paperwork, contracts, safety data sheets and passenger information. If your document is not on this list, send it over and we will confirm.

How important is translation in the logistics industry?

Goods cross borders with documents that customs officers, carriers and customers must all understand. Clear translation reduces delays, avoids disputes and keeps your contract terms consistent in every language.

Do you offer French to English translation for transport firms?

Yes. We translate between English and French in both directions, and we assign translators who work into their native language and know your subject. Send us a sample and we will confirm the best match.

Can you translate transport safety information?

Yes, our translators work on safety instructions and procedures for air, rail, road and sea transport. Tell us which regulator or customer will review the text, as some bodies set their own requirements.

How much does logistics translation cost?

Cost depends on the language pair, the length and complexity of the documents, the file format and your deadline. We quote per project, so send your files and you will receive a clear quote.
